title: AES Practical Security Margin
summary: Practical attacks reach reduced-round AES-256 variants but do not directly break standardized AES-128 or AES-256; determine the AES family's remaining security margin.

formal_statement.body: Determine how far the AES family is from practical insecurity, using about $2^{64}$ basic instructions as the practical-time threshold.

scope.domain: Practical cryptanalysis and attack-complexity assessment of the AES block-cipher family.
parameters: About 2^64 basic instructions: the practical-time threshold for evaluating attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the distance to practical insecurity through the best attack complexity on full AES and the proximity of practical reduced-round attacks to the standardized round counts.

citations.label: Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds

progress.summary: The paper presents AES's distance from practical insecurity as a crucial question and uses about 2^64 basic instructions as a practical-time benchmark. Its reduced-round AES-256 attacks narrow the margin but do not directly break standardized AES-128 or AES-256.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Key Recovery Attacks of Practical Complexity on AES-256 Variants with up to 10 Rounds
